_comment: Ratchet for bun run test:audit. Counts normally only go down: lower a number in the same commit that lowers the count. A number may go UP only when the DETECTOR got stricter and started seeing sites that were always there, never to admit new ones — raise it in the same commit as the detector change and record the reason below.
_wallClock: 0. The last ten sites went in one pass (see the PR that lowered this line). Each became either a BRACKET — two clock readings taken either side of the call, so the stamp is pinned to an instant inside them and no tolerance encodes machine speed — an EVENT ORDER (the estimator is released only after the route has answered; a shutdown marker due before the drain's own timer, which the event loop therefore always fires first), a WAIT rather than an assertion (the review-item precondition loops until the clock leaves the stamped millisecond, which slowness only makes arrive sooner), or a COUNT in the style of list-docs-linear.test.ts (paragraph re-scans, round trips, eager binds). Nothing was deleted to reach zero: every rewrite was shown red against a deliberately broken timing. A number here may go UP only if the detector gets stricter.
_sourceShape:
30. Was 42, and 42 was never a census (the history of why is in the PR that raised it from 36: the detector got stricter and surfaced six reads that were always there). What went this pass:

The NINE MCP tests that read packages/mcp/src through test/harness/mcp-source.ts now drive the built bundle over stdio instead — claim-warning, decision-line, declare-lead, nudge-line, plugin-version-reported, review-item-tools, stale-write-surface, tool-wiring, watch-coverage. The harness they used is deleted, not exempted. packages/mcp/test/harness/mcp-bundle.ts grew two fields for this — serverVersion and instructions off the initialize handshake — which is what a client actually sees. Every rewrite was shown red against a deliberately broken bundle, and SIX of the old source assertions stayed GREEN under the same break (a version bumped in src and manifest but never rebuilt; set_doc_content hard-coding confirmOverwriteHumanEdits; list_watched_docs fabricating a coverage all-clear; set_workspace_lead hard-coding takeover; the review payload forking behind the spread; archive_doc's dispatch arm made unreachable while its case label stays). Two more were FALSE POSITIVES: a behaviour-preserving respelling of claimNoticeFor(taskId) and of decisionAnsweredLine(p) turned the old greps red with nothing broken.

packages/widget/test/css-minify.test.ts carries a per-site `// audit: not-source` marker: styles.css there is the minifier's INPUT, not the subject — no assertion's expected value is a literal from the file. That third shape is now written into the marker's docstring in scripts/test-audit.ts, with the discriminator a reviewer should apply.

THE FLOOR IS 3, and they are named: decide-option-hover-css.test.ts (a :hover treatment), board-nav-widget-clearance-css.test.ts (a calc() of max() and env() happy-dom discards whole) and shell-grid-placement.test.ts (grid auto-placement, which needs a layout engine). They are PERMANENT and counted, not exempted. bun run ui:shot would render them for real, but it is a local dev tool — it needs a Chrome binary and a running server, and .github/workflows/ci.yml does not run it — so moving them there would retire the checks rather than convert them. Each file says so in its own header. If ui:shot ever runs in CI, convert them and take this to 0.

Two app tests converted so far: lazy-events.test.ts and load-beacon.test.ts both drive bootBoard through test/boot-harness.ts and read the fetches. lazy-events' old regex was ALREADY VACUOUS — it demanded an adjacency the real code never had and stayed green with the call reinserted in exactly that position. load-beacon's old form stayed green when the projection phase was dropped, when the network sums were dropped, and when the report was assembled and never sent.

WHAT REMAINS, all in packages/workspaces-app/test, all the same shape — read src/board/*.ts, app.ts, board-live-wiring.ts, doc-meeting-mount.ts or meeting-strip.ts as TEXT and assert on that text: board-mic-dock-css, board-model, board-quick-actions, board-source-contract, board-url-wiring, home-board-rows, home-nav-reset, huddle-entry, meeting-strip-css, parallelism-cap, review-criteria, review-item-comments.tsx, sentry-boot, walk-handoff, walk-return. bootBoard and bootApp have been exported since PR 634, so the honest reason these stay is that nobody has converted them yet.

Still invisible, so nobody reads 30 as a census either: a read whose path is in a constant declared elsewhere (review-item-tools.test.ts still reads a BUNDLE const that way), a support module outside a test/ directory, and require().
